result.note: Tests the US tariff legal shift (Section 122 and Section 301) and the Quad membership. The diplomatic mood and the energy pitch are skipped as soft.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about US trade measures affecting India, as of May 2026:
items: The US Supreme Court scrapped the "Liberation Day" tariffs, which had been the original basis for the India–US trade deal.
After the ruling, Washington imposed a flat duty of 18% under Section 122.
The US launched Section 301 investigations into Indian trade practices.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because the flat duty under Section 122 is 10%, not 18%. India–US trade talks stalled after the Supreme Court ruling, and US negotiators were expected in India in June 2026.
questions.source: Washington pivoted to a 10% flat duty under Section 122 and launched Section 301 investigations into Indian trade practices

questions.prompt: In May 2026, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio was due to attend a Quad foreign ministers' meeting. Which group of countries makes up the Quad?
options: India, the US, Australia and Japan
India, the US, Australia and South Korea
India, the US, Japan and the Philippines
India, the US, the UK and Australia
questions.explain: Rubio was to meet his counterparts from India, Australia and Japan at the Quad ministerial meeting. Despite the trade friction, the security imperative in the Indo-Pacific remains what holds the India–US partnership together.
questions.source: Rubio heads into a Quad ministerial meeting on Tuesday with counterparts from India, Australia, and Japan.
